answer_1.quote: We have used a final prompt for generation: "Task: Generate the text in {language_name} similar to the input social media text but using different words and sentence composition." ... This yields machine‑generated social‑media texts that are paraphrases of the original human posts.
answer_1.outputs: Machine‑generated social‑media texts (paraphrased) in 22 languages across 5 platforms

answer_2.quote: We have conducted similarity analysis between machine‑generated (3‑iteration paraphrased) and human‑written social‑media texts for individual generation models ... Metrics used include METEOR, BERTScore, n‑gram overlap, Levenshtein Distance, MAUVE and LangCheck.

answer_3.quote: We have used meta‑evaluation utilizing LLM judges to compare the quality of the generated texts of individual generators to the quality of original human texts ... We selected Gemma-2, Qwen2, and Llama-3.1 as meta‑evaluators for judging quality of the texts generated by the examined approaches.
methods: pairwise evaluation with majority voting among LLM judges

answer_4.quote: We have conducted manual human check of the generated texts, resulting in identification of various phrases indicating noise in the data such as "as an AI model", "language model", "instruction", "task", etc.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators inspected generated samples and marked any text containing obvious model‑failure phrases (e.g., boilerplate AI disclosures).
criteria: Presence of noise phrases (e.g., "as an AI model", "language model", "instruction", "task")
